A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

tumor promotion by a variety of different compounds in rat liver in the initiation/promotion paradigm is associated with an increase of the growth of normal liver and of the putative premalignant cell population.

tumor promotion in rat and mouse liver is due to the combined effects of increased cell replication and decreased cell death in normal and preneopalstic cells and that the increased cell replication is a consequence of the enhanced mitogenic activity of the tumor promoter on the one hand and of the proliferation advantage (shorter cell cycle time and/or longer cell survival) of the putative initiating event on the other hand.
all liver tumor promoters tested in our studies so far induce a proliferative response in preneoplastic cells.
